title: React Admin — plan-time crystallization
stack: React 19 · Vite · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 + shadcn · TanStack Router/Query · MSW v2 · Playwright + axe · Opus 5 orchestrator + Sonnet 5 mechanic sub-agents
about: Same task as workbench 02 — identical base app, entities, tiers, and batch schedule — so its sweeps serve as historical baselines. Both arms run the SAME autonomous light harness (plan → build → verify, HARNESS.md): an Opus orchestrator writes a plan artifact before any code, delegates mechanical implementation to Sonnet mechanic sub-agents, and closes the four gates itself. The only experimental variable is a plan directive present in the with-schematics arm: during planning, patterns repeating ≥3 times across the remaining schedule get a Project Builder schematic authored BEFORE implementation; everything below the threshold is hand-written. Schematic decisions are persisted in the plan file for post-hoc audit.
proves: That the win is the CRITERION, not the artifact. Workbench 02 showed blanket batch-1 schematization never amortizes (+48% cost, zero quality gain on the leveled sweep). If deciding WHERE to schematize at plan time beats it — a cheaper batch 1 than blanket schematics, an earlier cost crossover against the manual arm, and lower inter-batch variance — then the value of schematics lives in planning-time judgment over foreseeable repetition, and standardization is something you decide, not something you default to.
